A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SignViP. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation and back-translation experiments on RWTH-2014T and How2Sign, alongside ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds human evaluation, comparator results, initialization ablation, evaluation-model perturbation tests, and token-translation measurements.

M1.justification: The multi-condition encoder, diffusion model, FSQ autoencoder, and frame-level token translator retain their architectures, objectives, training procedures, and inference pipeline. The expanded Figure 2 caption explains the existing method.

E1.justification: The two datasets, sign languages, and generation task remain unchanged. Appendix E.4 adds corrupted-input scenarios for evaluating the back-translators: spatially and temporally perturbed poses and videos synthesized from those poses.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MoMP combined with ControlNet and with AnimateAnyone, substantially extending the end-to-end comparison to pipelines built around the strongest retained pose-production comparator. V1 evaluated MoMP only in pose back-translation. Existing video-generation comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds COMET evaluation, anonymized human similarity judgments from 10 participants, controlled pretrained-versus-scratch evaluation, perturbation sweeps, and normalized DTW on decoded condition embeddings. These substantially expand evaluation procedures; the original dataset splits, resolutions, training budgets, and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E.3–E.4 add an initialization ablation and tests of whether back-translation scores decrease with spatial and temporal corruption. Appendix G adds token-translation diagnostics using the existing compression and scheduled-sampling sweeps. Figure 4(e) also replaces the erroneous reconstruction-loss display.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's checklist answers yes to statistical-significance reporting but supplies no corresponding analysis. Human vote totals describe sample sizes and outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing headline scores are retained, but substantial results are added for COMET, MoMP pipelines, human judgments, initialization, perturbations, and DTW. SignViP receives 70.0% and 81.8% of human votes. Figure 4(e) replaces duplicated codebook-usage curves with reconstruction-loss results; compression-rate-2 ROUGE-L also changes from approximately 23.7 to 21.89 in Figure 4(a) and Table 10.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the FSQ formulation, and the mathematical description of the pipeline remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs. The added DTW and perturbation descriptions specify empirical evaluation procedures without introducing new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: fine-grained multi-condition tokenization improves sign-video generation, with state-of-the-art quality, temporal coherence, and semantic fidelity. V2 adds supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds targeted qualifications about pose-extraction errors, dependence on back-translator quality, nonexpert human evaluation, and temporal misalignment in token scoring. It interprets the new diagnostics as supporting evaluation reliability and pretrained initialization. The original multilingual-support and computational-efficiency limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies pretrained initialization of diffusion baselines and explicitly marks compression rate 8 as the selected setting. It documents human-evaluation instructions, perturbation construction, and the DTW embedding-comparison procedure. Core architecture details, hardware, hyperparameters, and the repository link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for COMET, translation evaluation, diffusion pretraining, additional generative methods, and pose-guided sign-video generation. It condenses the SignGen discussion, while preserving the central positioning around fine-grained conditions and discrete tokenization.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist, and appendix sections, updates author and affiliation information, and expands selected evaluation explanations. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact, with localized language corrections.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain columns and comparator rows; Tables 6 and 9–11 and perturbation Figure 5 are new. Figure 4 is redrawn with revised axes and a replaced reconstruction panel, and Figure 2's caption expands. Existing appendix tables and qualitative case figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evaluation by adding comparable MoMP-to-video pipelines, human visual-similarity judgments, and checks of back-translation sensitivity, addressing important gaps in v1's proxy-based evidence. It also corrects the misleading reconstruction-loss plot. The human study does not establish expert linguistic adequacy, statistical uncertainty remains unreported, and checklist statements conflict with the human study and statistical reporting. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in evidential support.
